To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a data trust is an entity that works within the law and provides ethical, architectural and legal support for trustworthy data stewardship, and that data trusts are therefore both liberating and constraining.
a data trust works within current law to provide ethical support and architectural and governance support to increase trust in the use and exchange of data for AI and other purposes.
data trusts work within the law to promote trust in data processing by providing ethical, architectural and legal support for trustworthy data stewards.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of data trusts as an approach to trustworthy data stewardship.

the following questions: How can data trusts be designed to be ethical, trustworthy, and legal? What are the ethical, technical and legal implications of data trusts? What are the legal implications of data trust? What is the relationship between law and data trusts? How do we build data trusts? How does a data trust operate? How do we ensure the data trust is trustworthy?
(a) the ethical and legal status of data trust; (b) the architecture of a data trust; and (c) how a data trust can be used to promote trustworthy data processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a data trust works within law to provide ethical and governance support to data stewards to ensure that their use of data is trustworthy.
a data trust works within and beyond the law to provide a framework for the ethical, architectural, and governance support of trustworthy data processing.

a data trust is a framework that is designed to be trustworthy, and that it provides a legal framework within which the trust can be implemented, and a set of ethical and architectural principles that guide the implementation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
data trusts are a way of making the data economy more trustworthy, and so of increasing the benefits that can be derived from the data economy.
we have shown how data trusts could be used to provide a framework that would enable trustworthy data processing, and we have identified the key elements needed to support this.

a data trust provides a framework within which a trustworthy data processor can be established, and within which a trustworthy processor can process data in a manner that is ethically acceptable, and that respects the legal requirements of the processor, the data provider and the data subject.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of a data trust, as we have developed it, is not a new one, but a rebranding of existing concepts, with the addition of some new ideas.
a data trust is a legal entity that provides the necessary conditions of trustworthiness for data processing, in particular by providing a governance structure that is both ethical and legal.
a data trust is not a legal entity but a set of agreements between data subjects, data controllers, data processors and data stewards that work within current law.
